references.text: Benjamin is described as a wolf that divides the spoil, reflecting the theme of sharing war plunder found in the Book of Judges.
The Israelites took women and spoil from the Midianites, similar to the expectation of spoil and women in Sisera's mother's speech.
Laws concerning women taken as spoil in war, reflecting the mindset of viewing women as war plunder.
David divided the spoil equally between those who fought and those who stayed behind, a theme regarding the distribution of war plunder.
The psalmist speaks of dividing the spoil, including colorful garments, which directly parallels the colored fabrics mentioned in Judges.
The virtuous woman makes embroidered rugs and fine clothing, similar to the embroidered garments mentioned as spoil.
The prophecy about sharing the spoil with joy, reflecting the expectation of dividing war plunder in the Song of Deborah.
